pending_commit.commit_message: cr50: use dedicated region for info1 accesses The INFO1 flash space is used for various purposes (endorsement key seed, Board ID and flags, serial number, etc.). Accessing these spaces in INFO1 is accompanied by managing the flash region registers, each time opening a window of the appropriate size, with appropriate permissions, etc, In fact none of these spaces contain a secret, to simplify things and preventing situations when concurrent accesses change the flash range window settings lets dedicate previously unused Region 7 register file to providing always open read access to INFO1. Write access will be enabled/disabled as required. In prod images write accesses will always happen from the vendor command context. In DBG images CLI commands will also have write access to INFO1. INFO1 window is accessed by other H1 based devices as well, this is why it is necessary to enable the window in the common chip code. BRANCH=cr50, cr50-mp BUG=b:138256149 TEST=the firmware_Cr50SetBoardId test now passes on Mistral. Calling reboot in this upstart script has no immediate impact. Thus, we wait an additional 60 sec after the already long update. Additionally, since reboot has no immediate impact, this script proceeds to unblocking the ui when it hits the "display_boot_message action restore_frecon" line. vm_tools: Put ARCVM processes in a proper cpu cgroup This CL bind-mounts host's |session_manager_container| cpu cgroup into Concierge. The cgroup is for Chrome to throttle Android processes (both ARC++ and ARCVM) based on its active window state etc. The CL also modifies Concierge's ARCVM code so that it adds ARCVM's crosvm process to |session_manager_container| group right after fork() but before execve(). With that, the first crosvm process and all its children will belong to the right cpu cgroup instead of the default one, /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/vms. Alternatives considered: Move ARCVM's crosvm process(es) somewhere outside Concierge. => This doesn't work well because the PID of crosvm Concierge knows is for Concierge's own PID namespace. The PID is useless outside Concierge, and the outside process in the init PID namespace has to scan through /proc/<pid> entries to find the crosvm process. Also, crosvm spawns threads and child processes after it's executed. Moving all of them without introducing races is a messy job. OTOH, if we change the crosvm's cpu cgroup before execve() (which is what this CL does), we don't have the race issue. However, this still left an edge case in which a socket has SO_BINDTODEVICE but does not have bind() explicitly called. However, lacking any oif rules, our set of policy rules has nothing to distinguish this source address selection case from regular source address selection. Therefore when the socket is bound to a device that is not the primary interface on the system, the bound device and the outcome of source address selection are in disagreement. This change adds a pair of oif rules for all interfaces so that source address selection takes any potential bound device into account. Adding this functionality required providing support for FRA_OIFNAME in shill. Note that all of our kernel trees define this routing policy type. UPSTREAM: mm: don't cap request size based on read-ahead setting We ran into a funky issue, where someone doing 256K buffered reads saw 128K requests at the device level. Turns out it is read-ahead capping the request size, since we use 128K as the default setting. This doesn't make a lot of sense - if someone is issuing 256K reads, they should see 256K reads, regardless of the read-ahead setting, if the underlying device can support a 256K read in a single command. This patch introduces a bdi hint, io_pages. This is the soft max IO size for the lower level, I've hooked it up to the bdev settings here. Read-ahead is modified to issue the maximum of the user request size, and the read-ahead max size, but capped to the max request size on the device side. The latter is done to avoid reading ahead too much, if the application asks for a huge read. With this patch, the kernel behaves like the application expects.
